I bought this to seal plastic zip locking bags for a business. The unit I received is identical to the pictures. It’s just under 6 pounds, 16 inch long, 3.5 inch wide. The sealing area is 12 inches long and makes a 1/4 (6mm) wide seal. Now, it looks like something from the 1970-1980’s with the color but the construction is quality for what it needs to do. It has a cast aluminum frame with rubber feet that holds steady on a table. It is made in China and the plastic parts reflect that, however, all screws are tight and the knobs and handles work well. The top arm is spring loaded with a central pivot and a rubber piece that provides even pressure across the seal area. The hinge on the top arm to the base is sturdy, slight wiggle side to side if pushed but the arm operates consistently up and down without issue. The unit is ready to go out of the box. The instructions are not translated to English very well. They did provide enough info to use some additional common sense to get started within minutes of unboxing. The dial on the front goes from 0-8 and is basically a timer. There is a red LED that indicates that the heating element is on. It only heats when the arm is pressed down and you will hear a clicking sound. The dial is similar to a seconds timer but slightly shorter. The heat level is unchanged. This is the real McCoy of reviews. I know this product front-to-back, it's positives and shortcomings. I used to work at an industrial aircraft part warehouse, and this product, in various lengths, was THE sealer we used. So I've operated this and the other length options THOUSANDS of times.
This is how it works: there's a piece of teflon tape on the bottom covering a wire heating element/filament. This flat wire is removable, as is the teflon strip, making replacement easy, which is good, as both do not last forever (think of a lightbulb filament, only one with much more electricity passing through it, and the teflon tape is only teflon-coated paper, which will burn and crack after a number of uses, possibly 100, depending on the heat level and care it is treated with). The heat is controlled by a dial knob. The element heats up when the upper bar is pulled down, which compresses the two plastic sheets. The thicker the sheets, the longer you need the bar down and the higher you need the heat. Again, the filament is on the bottom, and both sheet's need to be melted enough to adhere, so plan the heat level accordingly. I've sealed thin, sandwich bag-thick bags, bubble wrap, potato chip bags, as well as thick industrial strength vinyl bags.
The sealer's casing is of strong metal design, industrial, and durable to a moderate amount of disgruntled employee abuse (heh).
